issues.description: The template's StockIngredient class provides a getter named retrieveQuantity(), but the Stock class (in the template) calls getQuantity(). The problem statement also instructs students to add getters for private fields, implying the conventional getQuantity() name. This method-name mismatch within the template prevents the code from compiling and contradicts the expected getter name, blocking students from implementing the intended design.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the getter name consistent: rename StockIngredient.retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity(), or alternatively update Stock to call retrieveQuantity(). Prefer renaming to getQuantity() to match the problem statement's expectation and the solution implementation.

issues.description: The template defines the quantity getter for StockIngredient as retrieveQuantity(), while the solution (and the rest of the code) uses the standard getter name getQuantity(). The problem text requests adding getters for all private fields (implying standard getX names). This naming mismatch creates a mapping and compilation problem: students see/get instructions to add getters, the template provides retrieveQuantity, but Stock and the solution expect getQuantity, causing confusion and likely compile/runtime errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename retrieveQuantity() in the template StockIngredient to getQuantity() (and ensure other getters follow the getX convention) so the getter name matches the problem instructions and the usage in Stock and the solution implementation.
